chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Coleman Hawkins's arrival in 1923
summary: Willard says Hawkins came in 1923 with Mamie Smith and Harvey Brooks; Howard says he only tried to get a job and was scared by Hawkins's sound.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: You mentioned on the other tape that Coleman Hawkins came to Los Angeles in 1923 with Mamie Smith and Harvey Brooks.
And you two worked together quite a bit?
No, we didn't work together at all.
I was just trying to get a job, you know.
Uh-huh. So Harvey Brooks had worked with Coleman Hawkins quite a bit?
Yeah. Harvey Brooks had. Oh, yeah, Harvey Brooks played with a whole gang of good people.
Did he stay here very long, do you know, Coleman Hawkins, at that period?
Was he a great player at that time, too?
Yes, he was a very good player. Scared me to death with a horn, till I got in there, then it didn't scare me no more.
What do you mean, it scared you to death until you got in there?
Till I got in there and got to playing.
Uh-huh. He always had sort of a pretty big sound, though, didn't he? Seemed to be a very strong player.
